h_sam.text: Will the Accessories Pack for Saros 10 fit my robot?

c_n.text: Will it work with what I already own? Shop Counter is an Alexa+ add-on. Alexa understands what you mean, and the store answers for the facts.

m_n0.text: The Alexa+ MCP toolkit isn't open to hackathon builders, so this Echo Show is our own real MCP client, live on AWS. Maya shops at Satechi.

m_s1.text: I just got an iPhone 15 and a MacBook Air.

m_s3.text: Will this charger work with my phone?

m_n_tap.text: Voice first, not voice only. She taps Place order on the screen.

m_n1.text: Later, in a brand new session:

l_n.text: Account linking is real OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, the way Alexa+ links accounts.

s_n0.text: Remember Sam from the start? Earlier, at Satechi, he told Alexa about his robot.

s_s1.text: I have a Roborock Saros 10R and an iPhone 16.

s_n1.text: Now he's at Roborock, a different store.

s_s2.text: Will the Accessories Pack for Saros 10 fit my robot?

s_n2.text: He only said “my robot”. Alexa knew it was his Saros 10R, and the no is the store's own words.

t_n1.text: Under the hood, every step is real JSON-RPC. Alexa passes “my robot” as it was said, and our MCP server on AWS Lambda finds the Saros 10R in the closet, kept in DynamoDB.

t_n2.text: MCP Apps draw the screens, and an Agent Skill sets the rules. Eighty-one of eighty-one eval cases pass, with zero made-up facts.

f_n.text: Try it yourself, the link is on screen. Shop Counter: the store clerk who remembers your stuff.
